issues.description: The template's Main.java constructs Seal, Pig, and Goat with two parameters (e.g., new Seal("Clarabelle", "marine")), while the problem statement and UML indicate animals only have a name attribute and the solution uses single-argument constructors (e.g., new Seal("Clarabelle")). This mismatch in expected constructor parameters will confuse students about the correct constructor signatures to implement and may cause the provided Main to not compile if they follow the UML/specification.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the template with the UML/specification by updating template/Main.java to use single-argument constructors (name only), e.g. Seal("Clarabelle"), Pig("Doodle"), Goat("Buttinsky"); or, if two-argument constructors are intended, update the UML/problem statement and solution to document and implement those additional attributes and constructors.

issues.description: The template Farm.java declares singFarmSongVerse without an Animal parameter (the parameter is commented out: /*Animal animal*/), but the UML and solution define singFarmSongVerse(animal: Animal): void. This method-parameter mismatch prevents students from implementing singFarmSong() and from calling singFarmSongVerse for each animal as specified by the exercise.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the template method signature to include the Animal parameter to match the UML and solution: private void singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal) { ... } and update the method body to use that parameter. This allows singFarmSong() to iterate animals and call singFarmSongVerse(animal) as intended.

issues.description: Constructor signature mismatch for the animal classes: the template Main (starter code) instantiates Seal, Pig, and Goat using two-argument constructors (e.g., new Seal("Clarabelle", "marine")), while the problem UML and the solution implementation define/expect single-argument constructors that only take the animal name (e.g., new Seal("Clarabelle")). This inconsistency creates confusion about the required class API and which attributes must be initialized, making it harder for students to map the problem description to the template and final solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the constructor usage consistent across artifacts. Either update the template Main to use single-argument constructors (e.g., new Seal("Clarabelle"), new Pig("Doodle"), new Goat("Buttinsky")) to match the UML and solution, or explicitly document and implement the additional second attribute in the problem statement and in the solution classes (and name that parameter consistently) if the two-argument form is intended.
